title: Tenant micro-warmers and KV fingerprint probing for low-variance cold start reduction
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Dedicated tenants with bursty, tail-sensitive workloads still experience high P95/P99 cold-start variance despite existing warm pool efforts. Current warm pool allocation is coarse-grained (fleet-level) and doesn't prioritize small but latency-sensitive tenants, nor does it pre-prime small, high-value KV fingerprints that materially affect first-token latency for chat-style workloads.

Proposal: Implement 'tenant micro-warmers' — lightweight, per-tenant prewarmed lanes that keep a small number (1-3) of hot replicas in a micro-warm state for tenants that meet tail-latency or SLA thresholds. Combine this with KV fingerprint probing: lightweight probes that surface a tenant's critical KV keys (most-accessed prefixes and early attention cache keys) and pre-prime those entries into the shard-local KV cache during micro-warmer activation. The approach is hybrid: predictive (based on recent QPS, shape, and scheduled traffic) + reactive (short-lived micro-warmers triggered on a per-tenant surge).

Goals: reduce P95 and P99 cold-start latency variance by prioritizing warm budget toward tenants where it matters, keep steady incremental resource costs, and expose control-plane knobs (Console + API) for ops to set tenant SLOs and micro-warmer budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane API to opt a tenant into micro-warmers and set budget (0-3 micro-replicas)
Runtime: micro-warm lane implementation with fast spin-up (< 800ms additional TFLOP load) and KV fingerprint priming hooks
Telemetry: per-tenant P50/P95/P99 before/after and micro-warmer hit ratio metrics available in Console
Automated heuristic: tenant eligibility computed from 7-day QPS, 95th token latency variance, and SLA tags
Operational safety: memory and I/O budget enforcement with eviction fallback to regular warm pool
E2E test demonstrating >= 40% reduction in P99 for a synthetic chat tenant workload at the same cost envelope
comments: 2025-02-21 - Aisha Kaur: Kickoff notes — reviewed problem with PM and runtime leads. Decided to prototype micro-warmers as a control-plane-managed feature rather than fully-autonomic on day 1 to simplify rollback and audits. Action: Miguel + Priya to draft runtime API and prototype probe logic.

2025-02-26 - Miguel Alvarez: Initial prototype committed. Key trade-offs: doing selective layer preload (head+last transformer block) reduced IO by ~35% vs full weight preload but still recovered ~70% of latency benefits in our microbenchmarks. Recording PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7890

2025-02-28 - Priya Shenoy (PM): Design review feedback — require explicit tenant opt-in and per-tenant cost reporting visible in Console. Also requested a canary plan for Dedicated fleets to avoid cross-tenant noise. Added 'tenant-billing' integration to scope.

2025-03-02 - Eng review (Trent Bowman): Safety check — ensure KV probe uses read-only snapshot and never writes tenant data. Confirmed we will only probe prefixes with anonymized metrics and will not log raw tokens. Recommended adding a circuit breaker to stop probing on sustained errors.

2025-03-04 - Miguel Alvarez: Performance experiment summary — synthetic chat tenant with 150 qps bursts: baseline P99 cold-start = 820ms; with micro-warmers + KV fingerprint priming P99 = 470ms (43% reduction). Micro-warm resource delta measured at +0.9% GPU memory usage fleet-wide when enabled for 12 tenants per 1k. Dashboard: https://datadog.redwood/board/WM-41257

2025-03-05 - Aisha Kaur: Decided implementation plan: roll out alpha to internal customers, then closed beta for 10 external tenants. Add console toggle and billing line item. Next: implement telemetry counters and add RBAC check for enabling micro-warmers on tenant settings.

2025-03-05 - Design (Leila Park): UX wireframes uploaded for Console micro-warmer controls, cost preview, and per-tenant heatmap. Link: https://confluence.redwood/projects/DED/pages/WM-41257-wireframes
benchmarks: Baseline synthetic chat tenant (burst 150 qps): cold-start P99 = 820ms, P95 = 420ms
Prototype (micro-warmer + KV fingerprint probe): cold-start P99 = 470ms, P95 = 260ms
Resource delta: +0.9% GPU memory per-tenant enabled (measured on dedicated fleet small cluster)
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal tenants only, enable via org feature flag (runtime+control-plane) - 2 weeks
Beta: invite 10 external tenants with a support runbook and billing preview - 3 weeks
Canary: gradually enable on 1% of fleet traffic, monitor P99 and memory pressure, rollback on >10% unexpected errors
GA: enable as opt-in in Console with cost estimator and telemetry in runtime-1.20
risks: If KV probes are too aggressive, they may cause extra disk IO and increase contention on shard-level caches
Incorrect tenant heuristics could waste warm budget on low-impact tenants — mitigation: roll-up cost dashboard and automatic eviction
Privacy: ensure probes don't capture or store raw inputs; runtime must only use anonymized access patterns
